inputs.userGoal: Add Terraform to stand up Azure Government cloud infrastructure for the tactical Arc demo, including exact network, cloud, and edge resource groups; a VNet with Bastion; Entra-authenticated VPN access for a laptop and an edge device; AKS behind Application Gateway; ACR with managed identity; Service Bus for cloud and edge apps; and a resource group for Arc-managed edge devices.
subGoals: Security-first: private AKS, ACR, and Service Bus connectivity with managed identity and RBAC.
Hybrid connectivity: Entra/OpenVPN point-to-site for laptops and optional IPsec site-to-site for the edge network.
Azure Government compatible: sovereign identity endpoints, DNS suffixes, provider environment, and US Gov region defaults.
insightsApplied: existing-resource-group: preserve the existing Terraform address and align it to the requested cloud resource group.
existing-log-analytics: retain the workspace and extend it as the diagnostics destination.
existing-acr: retain the registry resource and harden it with Premium private connectivity.
existing-aks: retain the cluster resource and add private networking, workload identity, and Application Gateway ingress.
existing-aks-rbac: retain operator RBAC for the deploying identity.
existing-acr-rbac: retain managed-identity image pull access.

overallReasoning.summary: A single Azure Government VNet provides hybrid access and private service connectivity. WAF_v2 Application Gateway is the only public application ingress and is managed by the AKS ingress add-on. AKS, ACR, Service Bus, and monitoring remain in the cloud resource group; shared connectivity remains in the network resource group; the edge resource group is reserved for Arc onboarding.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: This secure demo baseline uses several fixed-cost services: Bastion Standard, VpnGw1AZ, Application Gateway WAF_v2, and Service Bus/ACR Premium. The architecture is single-region and does not provide regional disaster recovery. The edge-to-Service Bus path depends on S2S VPN and hybrid DNS. Application Gateway requires a versionless TLS certificate secret from an existing Azure Government Key Vault; the Terraform grants its user-assigned identity secret-read access but does not create or manage the certificate. Existing Terraform addresses are preserved, but changing the previously declared resource-group name and network shape can force replacement if this configuration has already been applied; inspect terraform plan and migrate state before apply in that case.

plan.validation: All dependency names resolve. Subnets are nonoverlapping and meet minimum sizes: Bastion /26, Gateway /27, Application Gateway dedicated /24, and AKS /20. Standard static public IPs pair with Bastion, VPN Gateway, and WAF_v2. ACR and Service Bus use Premium for private endpoints. AKS uses Azure CNI for AGIC and its pod/service ranges do not overlap the VNet or P2S pool. GatewaySubnet has no NSG. Managed identity and RBAC replace registry and messaging credentials.
